intro.heading: Lesson Snapshot
text: **Big Idea:** God makes promises to us, and He always keeps every one.
**Bible Story:** Noah and the rainbow — Genesis 9:13-17. After the flood, God set the rainbow in the sky as the sign of His promise.
**Memory Verse (KJV):** “He is faithful that promised.” — Hebrews 10:23
**Take-Home:** Each child leaves with a “Today, in Children’s Church I Learned” slip and their finished rainbow craft.

**Materials:** Paper plates, cotton balls, 7 colored paper strips per child (a traceable set for the 4s and 5s, blank for the 6s to 8s), glue sticks, markers, the printed promise list for reference, take-home slips.
**Note on reading:** Assume most of the room cannot read fluently. Every verse on the slides gets read aloud by the teacher, and the promise words on screen stay short.

intro.heading: Adapting Within the Room (ages 4–8)
text: Teach one lesson to everyone. These are small adjustments at the craft table and during discussion, not separate lessons.

**Ages 4–5:** Give them strips with the promise pre-written in light grey so they trace it. They glue the cotton-ball clouds and place the strips. During discussion, ask yes/no or point-to-the-color questions.

**Ages 6–8:** They write the promise and the KJV reference on each strip themselves. Give them the discussion question: “Which promise do you need to remember this week?” and let them answer out loud.
**Pair them up:** Seat an older child beside a younger one. The older reads the promise aloud while the younger finds the matching color. It keeps the older kids engaged and the younger ones moving.
**Memory verse:** Everyone learns the full verse with motions. The 4s and 5s will catch “He is faithful” first, and that is enough.

intro.heading: The Seven Promises (for craft strips & slides)
text: This is the master list. Same order as the rainbow, top strip to bottom.

**Red:** To care for and protect us. Psalm 121:7-8. The LORD shall preserve thee from all evil: he shall preserve thy soul. The LORD shall preserve thy going out and thy coming in from this time forth, and even for evermore.
**Orange:** To guide us. Psalm 32:8. I will instruct thee and teach thee in the way which thou shalt go: I will guide thee with mine eye.
**Yellow:** To forgive us. Hebrews 8:12. For I will be merciful to their unrighteousness, and their sins and their iniquities will I remember no more.
**Green:** To answer our prayers. 1 John 5:14-15. And this is the confidence that we have in him, that, if we ask any thing according to his will, he heareth us.
**Light Blue:** To always be with us. Hebrews 13:5. ...he hath said, I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee.
**Blue:** To send us the Holy Spirit. John 14:26. But the Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, whom the Father will send in my name, he shall teach you all things.
**Purple:** He has good plans for our lives. Jeremiah 29:11. For I know the thoughts that I think toward you, saith the LORD, thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you an expected end.

closing.heading: Reinforcement Game (if time allows)
text: **Promise Color Match.** Tape the seven colors around the room. Call out a promise — “God promises to forgive us!” — and everyone runs to the matching color. Speed it up as they get it. Last round, call the color and they shout the promise back. This works for the whole 4 to 8 range because it is movement first, reading never.

**Rainbow Line-Up.** Hand out the seven colored strips at random. Kids line up in rainbow order without talking, just holding up their color. Then go down the line and each child says their promise. Older kids can read theirs; younger ones repeat after you.

closing.heading: Closing Prayer
text: Dear God, thank You that You always keep Your promises. Thank You for caring for us, guiding us, forgiving us, hearing our prayers, always being with us, sending Your Holy Spirit, and having good plans for our lives. Help us remember Your promises this week. In Jesus’ name, Amen.

closing.heading: Parent Connection (write on the take-home slip or say at pickup)
text: Ask your child: “What is one promise God made to us?” Point to a color on their rainbow and let them tell you. Remind them: God always keeps His promises.

slides.title: God Always Keeps His Promises
slides.say: Good morning! Today we're learning about the promises God makes to us. Every single one, He keeps.

slides.text: A promise is when you say you WILL do something — and you mean it.
slides.say: Have you ever made a pinky promise? A promise means you can count on it. Some people break promises… but God never does.

text: It rained for 40 days and 40 nights.
Noah, his family, and the animals were safe in the ark.
slides.say: God told Noah to build a big boat. When the flood came, everyone inside was safe because Noah trusted God.

text: Then God put a rainbow in the sky.

scripture.text: “I do set my bow in the cloud, and it shall be for a token of a covenant.”

slides.say: When the rain stopped, God gave a beautiful sign — the very first rainbow. It was a picture of His promise.
The rainbow reminds us: what God says, God does. He has never broken a promise, and He never will.

slides.text: God has SO many promises for us. Let's find them in the rainbow!
slides.say: Every color of our rainbow holds a promise from God. Ready? Here comes the first one.

slides.text: God promises to care for and protect us.

scripture.text: “The LORD shall preserve thee from all evil.”

slides.say: God watches over you day and night. You are never on your own.

scripture.text: “I will instruct thee and teach thee in the way which thou shalt go.”

slides.say: When you don't know which way to go, God helps you and shows you the right path.

scripture.text: “Their sins and their iniquities will I remember no more.”

slides.say: When we do wrong and we're sorry, God forgives us completely and remembers it no more.

slides.text: God promises to answer our prayers.

scripture.text: “If we ask any thing according to his will, he heareth us.”

slides.say: God hears you every time you pray. He is always listening.

slides.text: God promises to always be with us.

scripture.text: “I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee.”

slides.say: God is with you at home, at school, everywhere. He never leaves.

slides.text: God promises to send us the Holy Spirit, our Helper.

scripture.text: “The Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost… he shall teach you all things.”

slides.say: God sends the Holy Spirit — the Comforter — to help us and teach us.

slides.text: God has good plans for our lives.

scripture.text: “I know the thoughts that I think toward you… thoughts of peace.”

slides.say: God knows your whole life, and His plans for you are good.
Look at all of it! Seven big promises — and God keeps every single one.
Let's say it together with motions. "He" (point up) — "is faithful" (hand on heart) — "that promised" (pinky promise). Again!
Let's say it together with motions. "He" (point up) — "is faithful" (hand on heart) — "that promised" (pinky promise). Again!

slides.text: Which promise do YOU need to remember this week?
slides.say: Maybe you need to know God is with you. Maybe that He forgives you. Pick one and hold onto it this week.

slides.text: Now let's finish our rainbow craft!
slides.say: Grab your rainbow. We're going to add each promise to the right color.
